rationale: C11 is an unmistakable country-substitution template for the child proclamation. It uses the same statutory recital, factual findings, eligibility determination, operative extension, date ranges, and closing language, with Norway replaced by Luxembourg and only immaterial punctuation and dating differences. C12 shares only general proclamation conventions, while C04 concerns a different extension mechanism and supplies no comparable language or structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas by the act of Congress approved July 17, 1946, 60 Stat. 568, the President is authorized ... to grant an extension of time ... for the renewal of trade-mark registrations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas by the act of Congress approved July 17, 1946, 60 Stat. 568, the President is authorized ... to grant an extension of time ... for the renewal of trade-mark registrations
shared_material.explanation: The opening statutory recital is essentially identical.

shared_material.child_excerpt: with respect to trade-marks of nationals of Luxembourg registered in the United States Patent Office which have been subject to renewal on or after September 3, 1939
shared_material.parent_excerpt: with respect to trade-marks of nationals of Norway registered in the United States Patent Office which have been subject to renewal on or after September 3, 1939
shared_material.explanation: The child directly adapts the same operative finding by substituting Luxembourg for Norway.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: because of conditions growing out of World War II, such disruption or suspension of facilities essential to compliance with the conditions and formalities prescribed with respect to renewal
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive factual and legal language is reproduced verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: such registrations which expired after September 3, 1939, and before June 30, 1947, until and including June 30, 1948
